item.title: The State of Global Development: Key Takeaways from UNGA 2026
item.description: UNGA 2026 showcased a development sector at a crossroads: shrinking aid budgets, rising Global South leadership, and persistent siloes. The path forward requires consolidating what works and collaborating effectively across sectors.

item.title: Trump’s Greenland Deal: Modest Gains, Lasting Costs
item.description: The U.S.-Denmark-Greenland defense agreement modestly strengthens U.S. Arctic posture and permanently binds Greenland to NATO. But those gains were largely available without coercion, and the Trump administration’s threats have caused lasting transatlantic damage.

item.title: What Should the U.S. Government Do in Response to the FBI Hack?
item.description: The theft of sensitive FBI data by a cybercriminal group is a long-term national security threat. It also offers a clear case for an urgent, targeted, and proportionate use of U.S. offensive cyber capabilities, sending a clear message on what is off-limits for cybercriminals.

item.title: What Should Korea’s Take on “The Asian NATO” Be?
item.description: An Asian NATO is unlikely to be institutionalized in the near future. However, keeping the issue alive can serve as an aspirational goal. That aspiration will push Korea to further strengthen all the layers of its multi-layered security architecture.

item.title: Time to Confront Escalating Russia-Iran Intelligence Cooperation
item.description: Russia-Iran intelligence and technology cooperation is escalating. It’s time for the United States to better prioritize confronting it.

item.title: Bridging the Gulf? Thailand and Cambodia Turn to UNCLOS
item.description: Thailand and Cambodia begin compulsory conciliation talks.

item.title: What Does the Greenland Deal Mean for North American Security?
item.description: CSIS experts examine the September 22 update to the Defense of Greenland agreement and what it means for Greenland, Denmark, the United States, and Canada amid renewed tensions.
